mechanism: Triple antithrombotic therapy - aspirin PLUS a P2Y12 inhibitor PLUS an oral anticoagulant - produces additive antihaemostatic effects and substantially increases major bleeding risk. The combination is frequently an intentional, time-limited regimen (e.g. post-PCI in atrial fibrillation).

management.prescriber_action: This alert is intended to fire ONLY when all three antithrombotics are present together (aspirin AND a P2Y12 inhibitor AND an oral anticoagulant); it must NOT fire on any 2-of-3 pair (e.g. aspirin+warfarin, or DAPT alone). Confirm the indication and planned duration of triple therapy (frequently intentional and time-limited after PCI/ACS, e.g. atrial fibrillation post-stent). Do NOT independently stop any prescribed antithrombotic. If the overlap is unplanned or unexplained, urgently escalate to the prescriber. Assess bleeding risk and gastroprotection.
management.monitoring: Bleeding surveillance; ensure a documented stop/step-down (de-escalation) plan exists.
management.patient_counselling: Report any bleeding promptly; do not add OTC NSAIDs or aspirin; adhere to the planned course.
management.duration: Triple therapy is usually deliberately time-limited; confirm the intended duration and de-escalation plan.
management.exceptions: Intentional, prescriber-directed triple therapy is confirm-and-monitor; only unplanned or unexplained overlap is urgently escalated.

mechanism: Additive serotonergic (pharmacodynamic) effect is the primary risk and is dose- and total-serotonergic-burden-dependent, so single-agent antitussive-dose dextromethorphan with an SSRI/SNRI carries low baseline risk. CYP2D6-inhibiting SSRIs (fluoxetine, paroxetine) add a pharmacokinetic component by reducing dextromethorphan clearance and raising its exposure. This is additive PD risk, NOT an absolute contraindication (contrast the non-selective MAOI pairing, which is a separate contraindication rule: dextromethorphan__maoi_nonselective).

management.prescriber_action: Short-course single-agent dextromethorphan at the antitussive dose is usually acceptable alongside an established SSRI/SNRI. Risk of serotonin toxicity rises with high or misuse (recreational) dextromethorphan doses, with CYP2D6-inhibiting SSRIs (fluoxetine, paroxetine) that raise dextromethorphan exposure, and when other serotonergic drugs are also present. Prefer a non-serotonergic antitussive if any of these apply or if the cough is not troublesome. Do not stop or alter the established SSRI/SNRI to accommodate an OTC cough remedy; refer to the prescriber if antitussive cover is genuinely needed in a higher-risk patient.
management.monitoring: Patient self-monitoring; no routine test. If dextromethorphan is used, watch for serotonergic features (agitation, tremor, myoclonus, sweating, fever) over the first day or two, especially at higher doses or with additional serotonergic drugs.
management.patient_counselling: Do not exceed the recommended antitussive dose and do not use dextromethorphan-containing products recreationally. Seek urgent help for agitation, confusion, tremor, muscle twitching or stiffness, sweating, fever, or a fast heartbeat. Keep taking your antidepressant as prescribed.
management.exceptions: Risk-dependent, not a flat contraindication: baseline risk with single-agent antitussive-dose dextromethorphan is low and rises with high/misuse dextromethorphan doses, CYP2D6-inhibiting SSRIs (fluoxetine, paroxetine), and additional serotonergic agents. Non-selective MAOIs are a separate, absolute contraindication (see dextromethorphan__maoi_nonselective).

management.monitoring: Closely monitor cardiac rhythm during initiation and titration when risk factors or medicines affecting cardiac conduction are present. The retained fragments do not establish a numeric QTc threshold or dose-specific schedule.

management.exceptions: Established specialist opioid substitution therapy or specialist-directed methadone analgesia must not be unilaterally stopped by the pharmacist. In some cases, lithium toxicity has resulted from interactions between a NSAID and lithium. fragments.text: Drugs that reduce the gastric acidity (e.g., acid neutralizing medicines such as aluminum hydroxide, or acid secretion suppressors such as H 2 -receptor antagonists and proton pump inhibitors) impair the absorption of ketoconazole from ketoconazole tablets.

Acid neutralizing medicines (e.g., aluminum hydroxide) should be administered at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after the intake of ketoconazole tablets.
Upon coadministration, the antifungal activity should be monitored and the ketoconazole tablets dose increased as deemed necessary.

After pretreatment with omeprazole, a proton pump inhibitor, the bioavailability of a single 200 mg dose of ketoconazole under fasted conditions was decreased to 17% of the bioavailability of ketoconazole administered alone.

fragments.text: The effects of fluconazole on the pharmacokinetics of the sulfonylurea oral hypoglycemic agents tolbutamide, glipizide, and glyburide were evaluated in three placebo-controlled studies in normal volunteers.
